root_idea.summary: The root denotes what is contrary to ṭayyib: badness, unsoundness, impurity, or repugnance, whether sensory, moral, or intellectual.
root_idea.development: The semantic range develops from defective or impure material, such as metallic dross and foul taste or odor, to corrupt words, beliefs, actions, persons, prohibited things, and harmful associations. The lexical tradition distinguishes خَبِيث, bad in itself, from مُخْبِث, associated with or producing badness.

qac_form_accounting.reason: The Form I perfect is a distinct Quran-attested verb.
This is the suitable masculine citation form for the Quran-attested adjective and substantive.
The feminine plural is an inflectional form of خَبِيث and is represented under the masculine citation headword.
The feminine singular and its Quranic broken plural are represented under the common adjective citation headword خَبِيث.

senses.definition: To be or become bad, foul, or deficient in quality.
senses.usage_conditions: In the Quranic occurrence, the verb describes land whose produce is bad or unproductive; the definition is stated neutrally because the lexical evidence also applies it more broadly to things that become خَبِيث.

senses.definition: Bad, corrupt, wicked, or morally and intellectually unsound; something or someone characterized by such badness.
senses.usage_conditions: The Quran applies this contrastively to bad persons and souls, corrupt deeds and choices, false or ugly words, disbelief, and other things opposed to ṭayyib. It may be substantivized and may appear in masculine or feminine forms and plurals.

senses.definition: Impure, repugnant, or prohibited things; what is not acceptable or wholesome.
senses.usage_conditions: This usage concerns things rejected as foul, unlawful, or contrary to what is good, including the Quranic contrast between the khabīth and the ṭayyib. It is not limited to a single physical object class.

senses.definition: In the construction تَعْمَلُ الْخَبَائِثَ, shameful or wicked acts, specifically intercourse between men.
senses.usage_conditions: This is a Quran-specific euphemistic construction explained as referring to the sexual practice associated with the people of Lot; it should not be generalized to every occurrence of خَبَائِث.

senses.definition: In الشَّجَرَةُ الْخَبِيثَةُ, a bad or evil tree, interpreted in the lexical tradition as a colocynth or dodder-like plant, and also associated with garlic, onion, or leek.
senses.usage_conditions: This is a Quran-attested expression in the supplied 14:26 occurrences. The alternative plant identifications are interpretive specifications of the expression, not a general restriction on the adjective.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of an odor or taste, to become foul, nauseating, or abominable; of the soul or stomach, to become heavy or agitated with a tendency to vomit.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This includes idiomatic expressions describing a disagreeable smell, taste, or bodily reaction.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To commit adultery or fornication with someone.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A derived verbal construction with بِها specifies the sexual partner.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a venomous reptile or similar creature, to be malignant, noxious, impure, or foul.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is an application to harmful or unclean creatures, distinct from the neutral sense of becoming bad.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To cause the soul or stomach to become heavy, nauseated, or inclined to vomit.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Form II is attested in the causative construction concerning something that produces this bodily reaction.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become characterized by badness or wickedness, or to have or take bad, deceitful, or corrupt companions and connections.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The derived form can describe either the subject's own condition or the bad character of the people associated with him.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To teach someone to be bad, wicked, or deceitful, and thereby render that person corrupt or depraved.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is the causative transitive use of the Form IV verb.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To pretend to be bad, wicked, or deceitful, or to affect or attempt such conduct.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The form may express a display or deliberate adoption of badness rather than an established character.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To deem or regard something as bad, impure, unclean, foul, or corrupt.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The form is used both for judging creatures such as serpents and scorpions unclean and for judging a word or dialectal variant corrupt.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Badness or any quality denoted by خَبِيث; the state of being bad, wicked, deceitful, or corrupt.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is an abstract noun and may also denote the condition of having bad companions or connections.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The state of having bad, wicked, or deceitful companions, friends, connections, or assistants.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is a specialized nominal sense associated with the derived social relation rather than merely with personal badness.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Adultery or fornication.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is a specialized use of the abstract noun for sexual misconduct.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The dross or impure residue of iron or silver when molten; by extension, an adulterating alloy or anything lacking goodness.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The figurative contrast is between refined metal or pure gold and its rejected residue.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Excrement, ordure, impurity, or filth.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is a concrete and technical extension of the notion of rejected impurity.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Unlawful capture, especially the capture of a person from a protected people as a slave.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The term concerns capture contrary to a treaty, league, or an inviolable right belonging to the captured people.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Illegitimate or adulterous descent; being born spuriously.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The expression لِخِبْثَةٍ is used of offspring attributed to adultery or fornication.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A bad, corrupt, base, wicked, deceitful, guileful, crafty, or cunning person.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This personal application is broader than any one Quranic contextual translation.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An adulterer or fornicator.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is a specialized personal application of the adjective.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A blamer, censurer, slanderer, or calumniator.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is a reported personal use centered on harmful speech about others.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of language, opprobrious, reviling, bad, or corrupt.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The adjective may describe either abusive speech or a word or dialect considered corrupt in authority or usage.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of religion, infidel or pertaining to infidelity.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is a figurative application to religious belief or affiliation.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of food, drink, medicine, pungent plants, blood, or similar things, disagreeable, impure, unlawful, injurious, or foul.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The particular application depends on the object: taste and odor, legal unlawfulness, impurity, or harmful effect. These classical specifications are broader than the supplied Quran contexts.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A person who takes bad, wicked, or deceitful companions, connections, or assistants.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is a conventional personal application distinct from simply being bad in oneself.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Having a heavy, heaving, or nauseated soul or stomach.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The phrase describes a disagreeable bodily state and is not a general psychological meaning of the adjective.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a well or receptacle, corrupt and corrupting what falls into it.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is a figurative description of a source that spoils its contents.

other_classical_meanings.definition: In the formula used when entering a privy, male and female devils; alternatively, infidelity, disobedience, wicked conduct, or evil qualities.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The alternatives reflect established interpretations of the idiom and should not be treated as ordinary unrestricted meanings of the plural nouns.

other_classical_meanings.definition: As a substantive, a bad or wicked quality, or a culpable action.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The plural خَبَائِثُ may denote bad qualities or culpable acts; wine is idiomatically called the mother of such qualities.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Foul, filthy, or unclean creatures that were traditionally regarded as unsuitable for eating, such as vipers, scorpions, lizards, beetles, and mice.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is a culturally specified dietary classification, not a general restriction on every use of خَبَائِث.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Very bad, wicked, or deceitful; one much addicted to adultery or fornication.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The doubled pattern is an intensive personal adjective.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Worse, worst, or most wicked and deceitful.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: It may be used of people collectively or comparatively of a word or dialectal variant.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A conventional paired expression for bodily impurities, especially urine and human excrement; variant explanations include vomit and ordure, or other paired sources of distress.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is a fixed technical expression used in contexts of bodily relief or discomfort.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A state or situation that has become bad, corrupt, disapproved, or otherwise disordered.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The form occurs in the idiom وَقَعَ فِي وَادِي تُخُبِّثَ, meaning to fall into such a condition.

other_classical_meanings.definition: One who teaches or causes others to become bad, wicked, or deceitful.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This active-participial use focuses on producing bad character in others.

other_classical_meanings.definition: According to a reported extension, one who attributes or imputes badness or similar faults to others.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is an explicitly reported secondary application, retained as a lexical possibility rather than treated as the primary sense.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A cause of evil or corruption; of food, something that causes heaviness or nausea, or that is unlawful.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The noun denotes a source or cause of bad effects, with the food use specifying bodily or legal harm.

cautions: The Quranic nominal groups are consolidated under the citation headword خَبِيث; feminine and plural forms remain represented in the occurrence count and examples.

The lexical evidence uses an older Quran-reference convention for the tree expression. The modern 14:26 assignment in the public examples relies on the independently supplied QAC word locations, not on mechanically converting that historical citation.
